subject: System Design
title: Happens-Before Relationship
description: Learn Happens-Before Relationship in one minute.

hook.text: Event A sends a message. Event B receives it. A happened before B — we know this for certain.

buildup.text: The happens-before relation defines causal ordering: A → B means A could have influenced B.

discovery.text: If neither A → B nor B → A, the events are concurrent. No observer can determine which came first.

twist.text: Concurrency doesn't mean simultaneous. It means neither event could have caused the other.

climax.text: Happens-before is the foundation of reasoning about distributed systems. It replaces time with causality.

punchline.text: Causality, not time, defines event ordering.

quiz.question: What does 'concurrent' mean in distributed systems?
options: Neither event could have caused the other
Both happened at the same time
Both ran on the same server
